sentences.text: Mariliasuchus is an extinct genus of crocodyliforms classified as a notosuchian from the Late Cretaceous, belonging to the parent group Sphagesauria.
Unlike modern crocodiles with upward-facing nostrils, Mariliasuchus had nostrils located on the front of its skull, while its eyes faced laterally instead of upwards.
This animal possessed a highly modified dentition consisting of incisiform, caniform, and molariform teeth, with the front teeth directed horizontally rather than vertically.
Unlike modern crocodiles, Mariliasuchus lived primarily on land.
The enamel structure suggests it may have eaten plants, and microstructure indicates an omnivorous diet that included feeding on hard objects.
Studies show that as Mariliasuchus grew, its skull became shorter, more resistant, and laterally compressed.
The first remains of Mariliasuchus were collected in 1995 by the Brazilian paleontologist William Nava.
A second species, Mariliasuchus robustus, was named in 2007.
Fossils of Mariliasuchus have been discovered in close association with eggs, eggshells, and coprolites.
Fossils collected by William Nava were stored at the National Museum of Brazil but were partially destroyed in the 2018 fire.
Mariliasuchus had strong jaw muscles, suggesting significant mandibular activity.
Researchers inferred that Mariliasuchus had a sprawling posture and possibly amphibian habits similar to modern crocodilians.
The postcranial skeleton of Mariliasuchus mixes traits found in terrestrial Cretaceous crocodyliforms and aquatic eusuchians.
In adult Mariliasuchus, the eye socket arrangement is less circular than in juveniles.
The function of Mariliasuchus's horizontal front teeth is unclear, though comparisons with pigs suggest convergent dietary preferences.
Mariliasuchus fossils come from the Adamantina Formation and date to the Late Cretaceous, possibly the Campanian or Maastrichtian stages, living between 83.6 and 66 million years ago.
It is debated whether variations in Mariliasuchus specimens represent ontogeny, sexual dimorphism, or a separate species.
